question: Must spheres have infinitely many genuinely different closed geodesics?
idea: A closed geodesic is a loop that follows the metric’s straightest paths. The claim says every smooth Riemannian sphere of dimension at least two has infinitely many with distinct images, not just repeated laps of one loop. It extends to the stated spherical covers and all closed three-manifolds.
why: The study of smooth shapes, curvature, and how geometry changes from point to point.

glossary.meaning: A prime is a whole number greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself.
A space that looks like ordinary flat space when you examine a sufficiently small neighborhood.

exactClaim: Proves that every smooth Riemannian metric on Sn, n ≥ 2, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The same conclusion holds on every closed manifold admitting a finite smooth spherical cover and on every closed three-manifold, without orientability or nondegeneracy restrictions.
